title: Language Models as Measurement Apparatus for Culture

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring disparities in conversational agency by analyzing thread initiation rates and classifying interactional roles (speaker, addressee, side-participant) between male and female characters in film and television dialogue.

Quantifying deviations from learned stereotypical relationship norms (e.g., predicting two brothers as a married couple) to formalize and identify queer relationalities and subversion in scripted dialogue.

Evaluating how models internalize and rely on cultural norms and memorized character identities by comparing classification performance on original versus anonymized TV scripts (erasure) and measuring adaptation to historical text archetypes (attunement).
